source.title: Référentiel technique et technico-économique — Filière oléagineuses

quote: le colza n'a pas d'exigence particulière, le colza valorise bien les précédents riches mais s'accommode facilement derrière une céréale à paille
translation: Rapeseed has no particular requirement; it makes good use of rich predecessors but adapts easily behind a straw cereal.
interpretation: A straw cereal (durum/bread wheat, barley) is named as an easy, workable predecessor for rapeseed. This is phrased as tolerance, not an exclusive preference, so record it as the preferred family rather than the only acceptable one.
applicabilityNote: General ONCA oilseed guidance, not Tadla- or region-specific. The same page also says rapeseed is itself a good predecessor to wheat, which is a separate (forward) relationship, not recorded here.

source.title: Référentiel technique et technico-économique — Filière cultures maraîchères

locator: PDF page 42 (pdftotext page split, re-verified 2026-11-06), potato chapter, tuber-moth protection section
quote: en principe, une bonne rotation amène la pomme de terre sur le même terrain tous les 5 ou 6 ans
translation: In principle, a good rotation brings potato back to the same field only every 5 or 6 years.
interpretation: Stated as general good practice inside a passage about protecting tubers from the potato tuber moth, not as a disease-specific exception. Keep the 5-6 year range rather than picking one endpoint.
applicabilityNote: The same paragraph separately advises against growing potato near eggplant fields (field-to-field proximity, to limit shared pest movement) — that is a spatial-neighbour rule, not a predecessor-crop rule, and is NOT recorded as C.potato.prohibited_predecessor. No prohibited-predecessor fact was found for potato in this source.

source.title: Fiches techniques V: La tomate, l'aubergine, le poivron, le gombo — Bulletin 100
source.publisher: Ministère de l'Agriculture et du Développement Rural / PNTTA / IAV Hassan II

locator: PDF page 3 (pdftotext page split; the PDF is OCR'd from a 3-column bulletin layout and pdftotext reads columns out of strict order, so the quote below is the exact text as extracted even though neighbouring sentences on the same page belong to other columns)
quote: L'installation de la culture [aubergine] est la même que pour le poivron. ... Il est très exigent en rotation des cultures. La dissémination rapide de beaucoup de maladies interdit la monoculture. Les meilleurs rendements sont obtenus dans les terrains vierges ou nouvellement acquis, n'ayant pas été occupés par une autre solanacée pendant les 4 ou 5 dernières années.
translation: Eggplant is established the same way as pepper. ... It is very demanding in crop rotation. The rapid spread of many diseases rules out monoculture. The best yields are obtained on virgin or newly acquired land that has not been occupied by another solanaceous crop for the last 4 or 5 years.
interpretation: The bulletin explicitly states eggplant culture practice equals pepper's immediately before this passage, so the rotation requirement is read as applying to both. Corroborates, with an independent source, the catalog's existing C.eggplant.minimum_return_interval (5 years, Solanaceae, from pntta-roots.pdf, nematode management) — two sources now agree on a ~4-5 year Solanaceae break for eggplant.
applicabilityNote: OCR column-interleaving on this page makes attribution between the eggplant and pepper paragraphs imperfect; treat as a shared Solanaceae-family rule for both crops rather than an eggplant-exclusive statement. Research evidence only.
